what: Lockheed Martin is the largest defence contractor in the world. It builds the F-35 fighter, missiles and missile-defence systems, military helicopters and satellites, and it maintains those systems for decades after delivery.
customers: The US government is by far the largest customer, mainly the Department of Defense; allied governments buy through foreign military sales.
money: the F-35, F-16 and F-22 fighters and classified aircraft programmes
PAC-3 interceptors, HIMARS, JASSM and other precision weapons
Sikorsky helicopters, naval and radar systems
satellites, strategic missiles and space exploration work
moat: Programmes that take decades to qualify for, security clearances, and installed systems that need its own parts and servicing for thirty or more years.
risks: Almost all revenue depends on US government budgets and political decisions
Fixed-price development contracts have produced large losses before
F-35 delivery and upgrade delays affect both revenue and reputation
Newer, cheaper autonomous systems challenge its traditional platforms
opportunities: European and Asian rearmament is lifting foreign demand for fighters and missiles
Missile and interceptor production is being expanded to refill stockpiles used in recent conflicts
Decades of maintenance on each delivered aircraft provide revenue long after the sale
watch: F-35 deliveries and the backlog figure, which shows work already under contract.
